title: SLA-aware capacity simulator and right-size recommendations for Dedicated pools
creator: Amina Patel
description: Build a capacity simulation and recommendation engine tailored to Dedicated GPU pools that can: (1) ingest production traces or synthetic workload profiles, (2) simulate autoscaling policies and throughput guarantees under candidate pool sizes, instance types, and padding values, and (3) output right-sizing recommendations that balance cost and SLA attainment. The simulator will be SLA-aware (target p99 latency and target throughput) and support an operator-facing UI in Console plus a CLI for batch analysis. Key use cases: conservative reserve sizing for enterprise customers, automated suggestions for resizing commitments, and pre-deployment validation for new autoscale rules.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator can replay 7 days of anonymized request traces and produce expected p50/p95/p99 latency curves for a given Dedicated pool config
Recommendations engine produces a ranked list of 3 right-size proposals with estimated monthly cost, expected SLA attainment probability, and recommended autoscale policy parameters
Console view exists that shows input workload, simulation results, and 'apply recommendation' button that opens a follow-up ticket or creates a proposal PR to governance
Telemetry hooks added for per-pool metrics: qps, request queue depth, batch size distribution, KV cache hit rate, GPU utilization, and per-request latency histogram
End-to-end tests cover at least two autoscaling policies (utilization-based and queue-depth-based) against a small synthetic trace and validate predicted vs observed p95 within 15%
Documentation created: runbook for running simulations, explanation of recommendation heuristics, and privacy note on trace anonymization
comments: 2025-10-09 - Amina P: Initial ticket created after a customer call where Dedicated pool overcommit caused repeated p99 breaches. Scope: simulator + right-size recommender + Console integration.

2025-10-10 - Diego N: Spike completed to validate that replaying compressed traces (sparse token counts + arrival timestamps) gives stable latency predictions for sequence lengths up to 512. Found that batching model in runtime needs a simple 'effective batch factor' parameter for accurate simulation.

2025-10-11 - Eng leads: Decided to support two autoscale policy families in v1: utilization-based (GPU%) and queue-depth-based (pending requests threshold). We'll add support for mixed policies later.

2025-10-13 - Design review by Sofia M: Console mockups reviewed; suggested adding a 'confidence' badge on each recommendation and an explanation panel that shows main drivers (e.g., peak bursts, average queue length, KV cache hit rate).

Marking security_review_required=false for product code but will open a separate Sec ticket if we transfer traces across boundaries.

2025-10-15 - Diego N: Integration plan with fleet telemetry: query from metrics DB (ClickHouse) for aggregated per-pool 30d windows, then downsample to representative traces. Prototype script: https://github.com/redwood-inference/capacity-sim/pull/12

2025-10-16 - Product feedback from Elena R: Add an explicit 'safety margin' slider (0-30%) to recommendations and a toggle to prefer cost savings vs SLA headroom. PM wants default to conservative 10% for enterprise customers.

2025-10-17 - Progress: Core simulator single-node implementation produces latency predictions within 12% of observed p95 on replayed production traces for two test customers. Moving to multi-node and autoscale simulation next. Creating follow-up sub-issues for Console work and E2E tests.
implementation_notes: Simulator core will model: arrival process (trace or synthetic), batching efficiency curve (function of inter-arrival times and target batch window), per-token service time distribution, KV cache hit multiplier, and autoscale decision loop with cooldowns.

Right-size heuristic: enumerate candidate pool sizes from 25% to 200% of current commit in sensible steps, simulate 30-day trace for each, compute cost and SLA attainment probability, then rank by 'expected monthly savings per % SLA loss' and apply safety margin.
Autoscale knobs to expose: min/max pool size, scale step, cooldown, target utilization, target queue depth, burst capacity policy, and preferred instance family (A100/V100/H100 or equivalent).
Privacy: traces will be anonymized by removing request IDs, user IDs, and then compressing timing buckets. Option for customers to submit traces via private S3 for on-prem simulation.
Rollout: internal beta with two pilot customers (account managers assigned), then gradual enablement in Console as 'Recommendations (beta)'.
